meta.title: Ved Vidyalaya Foundation · A living Gurukul for the Vedas, Sanskrit and a full education
meta.description: In a quiet Gurukul, children learn the Vedas by heart from a teacher, speak Sanskrit, and study the modern subjects every child needs, free of charge. Help keep a voice older than writing alive.

hero.eyebrow: Ved Vidyalaya Foundation · A living Gurukul
hero.h1: Some things are too precious to write down. They must be remembered.
hero.lede: In a quiet Gurukul, children wake before the sun to learn the Vedas the only way they have ever been learned: from a teacher, by ear, by heart. Every lesson, every meal, every lamp is given freely. We exist so that this voice, older than writing, is never left to fall silent.
hero.trust: Every student learns free of charge · Sustained entirely by people who care
hero.artAlt: Dawn over the Gurukul: a sun rising behind a horizon line, with a single lamp flame in the foreground

ticker.text: A meal cooked and shared together

promises: Every lesson, meal and bed is free of charge
Taught by ear and by heart, as it always has been
No payment gateway: what you give arrives whole
Visitors welcome at the dawn recitation

why.h2: The Vedas were never written to be read. They were sung to be remembered.
why.lede: For most of human history the Vedas lived nowhere but in people: in the breath of a teacher and the memory of a child, carried forward one morning at a time with every tone and pause intact. A book can be reprinted. A voice, once it goes quiet, cannot. Each tradition survives for exactly as long as there is a child learning it.

cards.title: When a reciter passes
cards.body: When an elder dies without a student, a library closes that no one can reopen. Our whole work is to make sure there is always a student, sitting on the floor at dawn, ready to receive it.

cards.title: A child's voice is the archive
cards.body: No recording holds the Veda the way a trained memory does: living, correcting, able to teach. The children here are not studying a heritage. They are the heritage, continuing.

cards.title: Free, so no one is turned away
cards.body: No family pays a rupee. A child from the smallest village can become the ācārya the next generation learns from. That is what your gift makes possible.

programs.label: The Veda
programs.title: The Veda, by heart
programs.body: Students learn their Veda the way it has been learned for millennia: line by line, from a teacher, with every svara in place. Nothing is written down, so nothing can be lost, as long as there is someone to receive it.
points: Morning and evening recitation with the ācārya
Saṁhitā, pada and krama, each in its turn
Tested by ear, by visiting scholars
programs.caption: Morning pāṭha

programs.label: Sanskrit
programs.title: A language, spoken
programs.body: Sanskrit is spoken here, not merely studied. Grammar, poetry and the great texts become living things when a child can argue in them, joke in them and pray in them.
points: Spoken Sanskrit from the first week
Grammar through Pāṇini, poetry through kāvya
programs.caption: Grammar at noon

programs.label: Modern learning
programs.title: No door closed
programs.body: A Vedic education must leave every door open. Students also study English, mathematics, science and computing, so that they leave able to teach, to earn and to choose their own path.
points: A full school curriculum beside the Veda
programs.caption: Afternoon lessons

programs.label: A way of living
programs.title: Character, lived daily
programs.body: Sandhyā at dawn and dusk, the fire tended every day, the kitchen, the garden and the cows cared for by all. Discipline here is not imposed. It is absorbed, the way a language is.
programs.caption: Evening seva

shanti.deva: सह नाववतु । सह नौ भुनक्तु । सह वीर्यं करवावहै । तेजस्वि नावधीतमस्तु मा विद्विषावहै ॥
shanti.iast: saha nāvavatu, saha nau bhunaktu, saha vīryaṁ karavāvahai, tejasvi nāvadhītam astu, mā vidviṣāvahai
shanti.translation: May we both be protected. May we both be nourished. May we work together with vigour. May what we study be luminous. May we never hold ill will toward one another.
shanti.note: Śānti-mantra · recited by teacher and student before every lesson

keeps.kicker: What a single Gurukul keeps alive
keeps.h2: None of it can be stored. All of it must be practised.
keeps.lede: Four things that exist only while someone, somewhere, is doing them every day.

items.title: The sound
items.body: Every accent and every pause of the Veda, carried in living memory, exactly as it was received.

items.title: The language
items.body: Sanskrit as a spoken tongue, argued in, joked in, prayed in. Not a museum piece.

items.title: The fire
items.body: The agnihotra at dawn and at dusk, tended by children's hands, day after day without a break.

items.title: The way
items.body: Simplicity, service, and reverence for every living thing, learned by living it rather than by being told.

day.lede: Choose an hour. The rhythm has not changed in centuries; the mathematics textbook is the only new thing in the room.

moments.title: The Gurukul wakes before the birds
moments.body: Cold water, a clean dhoti, and the first sound of the day is the Gāyatrī, chanted together on the verandah while it is still dark.

moments.title: Two hours with the ācārya
moments.body: He recites a line. The students repeat it, twice forward, then in pairs of words, then in the krama order. Nothing is written down. Nothing is forgotten.

moments.title: Grammar, then mathematics
moments.body: Pāṇini first, algebra and science after. The same children, two worlds, one desk, and a surprising amount of laughter.

moments.title: A meal cooked by the students
moments.body: Each week a different group runs the kitchen. Everyone eats together on the floor. Nothing is wasted; the cows get the rest.

moments.title: Games until the light goes
moments.body: Kho-kho, kabaddi and cricket in the field. Teachers join in. It is loud, and it is meant to be.

moments.title: The day closes as it began
moments.body: Fire and sound. Then dinner, an hour of quiet revision, and sleep early enough that before dawn does not hurt.

moments.h2: Photographs and films from the Gurukul
moments.lede: New pictures and short films are added through the year: a festival, an examination, the monsoon, a new student's first morning.

voices.h2: From the people who know it best

give.h2: Of all the gifts a person can give, the tradition names one above the rest.
give.translation: “Of all gifts, the gift of sacred knowledge is the most excellent.”
give.body: There is no payment gateway and no middleman. What you give goes straight to the Gurukul and becomes a meal before the first recitation, oil for the evening lamps, a teacher's dakṣiṇā, a roof that holds through the monsoon. Give what you can, once or every month. Each rupee is a syllable kept alive.
give.letterCta: Read the letter from the Gurukul
give.remark: Add your name in the remark if you would like us to write and thank you.

visit.h2: Come and stand in it at six in the morning.
visit.body: No page can do what one morning in the Gurukul does. Visitors are welcome at the dawn recitation and at the midday meal. Write to us a week ahead and we will arrange the rest.
